stories.headline: Tajikistan begins withdrawal from International Criminal Court, fourth state to do so
stories.dek: The one-year process started on Friday, when Vladimir Putin stopped in Tajikistan after meeting Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China, Tajikistan's government said.
stories.summary: Tajikistan has formally begun leaving the International Criminal Court, joining Chad, Venezuela and Naoero in withdrawing since the US called for states to quit the court. The ICC said it regrets the decision and that it does not erase obligations incurred as a member.
body: Tajikistan has formally begun withdrawing from the International Criminal Court, becoming the fourth country to do so since the United States launched a diplomatic push to "dismantle" the court, the Presidency of the ICC's governing body said in a statement on Monday.

Tajikistan's government said it started the one-year withdrawal process on Friday, when Russian President Vladimir Putin made a stopover visit after a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to DW. The ICC issued an arrest warrant for Putin in March 2023.
Chad, Venezuela and Naoero, a Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru, have also announced withdrawals since the US called on countries to leave the court in July, The Hindu reported.

The ICC said it "regrets" Tajikistan's decision. It said the move risks undermining "the collective pursuit of justice" and weakens "global efforts to end impunity". The statement added that withdrawing does not release a state from obligations incurred while it was a party to the treaty.
"The ICC stands at the heart of the international system of accountability, and its effectiveness depends on sustained and unequivocal support from the international community," the court said.

Al Jazeera reported that the ICC found in March that Tajikistan had failed to comply with a request to arrest Putin. The Hindu said the court criticised Tajikistan for not detaining him when he visited in 2025. Putin is wanted over alleged war crimes in Ukraine.

DW reported that Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have accused the court of abusing its jurisdiction. It said Trump attacked the ICC in remarks at the Shenzhen meeting, drawing a smirk from Putin.
The ICC has 125 member states. That figure still includes the seven states that have formally started withdrawing, a process that takes a year to complete.
keyFacts: Tajikistan began its one-year ICC withdrawal process on Friday, according to its government.
Chad, Venezuela and Naoero have also announced withdrawals since the US call in July.
The ICC has 125 members, including seven that have begun withdrawing.
Tajikistan signed the Rome Statute in 1998 and ratified it in 2000.
The ICC issued its arrest warrant for Vladimir Putin in March 2023.
stories.background:
The ICC prosecutes individuals accused of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and the crime of aggression when national courts are unwilling or unable to act.

Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger announced their exits the previous year, denouncing the court as an instrument of "neocolonial repression".
stories.whyItMatters: Withdrawal takes a year to complete, so Tajikistan remains bound by the treaty until then, and the ICC says obligations incurred as a member continue afterwards.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in $43.9 billion all-stock deal
stories.dek: Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share they hold, and the deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028.
stories.summary: CrowdStrike agreed on Monday to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in stock, its largest acquisition to date. CrowdStrike shares fell 10% while Zscaler rose more than 15%.
body: CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at $43.9 billion, the companies announced on Monday, combining two cybersecurity firms as artificial intelligence is used to mount more attacks.

Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share, according to CNBC. The deal is subject to regulatory approval. CNBC reported it is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028, and TechCrunch described that as around this time next year.
Shares of CrowdStrike fell 10% on Monday, while Zscaler shares rose more than 15%, CNBC reported.

CrowdStrike, based in Austin, Texas, secures computers, phones and other devices connected to company networks. Zscaler, based in San Jose, California, provides cloud security products to about 8,000 enterprise customers, including zero-trust technology that requires users to authenticate each time they access an internal system.

The companies said the combination would unite CrowdStrike's endpoint protection software with Zscaler's zero-trust platform to better defend customers against data breaches. They also said it would help customers adopt AI safely.

"With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement.
The deal is CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date, CNBC reported. The two companies had a combined market value above $265 billion at Friday's close, behind Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.
Analysts at JPMorgan wrote that adding Zscaler could bring more breadth as vendors consolidate and position CrowdStrike for rising demand for what they called "AI Sovereignty".

CrowdStrike also reported fiscal third-quarter earnings of 34 cents per share on $1.58 billion in revenue on Monday. LSEG had forecast 31 cents per share on $1.53 billion. Zscaler's fiscal first-quarter results, also released on Monday, beat estimates, CNBC reported.

Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share.

stories.background:
CNBC reported that cybersecurity dealmaking has been heavy this year. Google announced plans last year to buy Wiz for $32 billion, and Cisco paid about $28 billion for Splunk in 2024. Palo Alto Networks closed a $25 billion deal for CyberArk earlier this year.

CrowdStrike shares have risen about 80% this year as of Monday's open, CNBC reported, as demand for AI security has grown.
stories.whyItMatters: The deal would give CrowdStrike a network security business and narrow its gap with market leader Palo Alto Networks, according to analysts cited by CNBC. Enterprise customers of both firms would be offered a combined product.

stories.headline: Tata Steel buys APL Apollo stake in block deal; combined market value falls ₹30,707 crore
stories.dek: Shares of both companies fell on Monday, with APL Apollo down 21.4 per cent, after a two-part deal that includes an open offer at ₹2,301.40 a share.
stories.summary: Tata Steel bought 2.77 crore APL Apollo Tubes shares for about ₹5,825 crore on Monday, the first step in a larger deal. Both stocks fell, and the two companies together lost ₹30,707 crore in market value, according to Business Standard.
body: Tata Steel bought 2,77,38,075 shares of APL Apollo Tubes, worth about ₹5,825 crore, in block deals on Monday from promoter group entity S Gupta Holding Private Limited, at ₹2,100 a share, according to BSE data.

Tata Steel fell nearly 8.2 per cent, the biggest percentage loser among Sensex and Nifty 50 constituents, Business Standard reported. CNBC put the fall at over 9 per cent during the session. APL Apollo settled at ₹1,668.15, down 21.39% from its previous close of ₹2,122.15, and was the worst-performing midcap stock. Together the two companies lost ₹30,707 crore in market value, Business Standard said.

The block deal is the first of three tranches under a share purchase agreement dated November 23. S Gupta Holding will sell its entire 7,38,60,062 shares, which APL Apollo describes as 26.38% on a fully diluted basis, to Tata Steel at ₹2,100 each. The second tranche is 3,33,19,009 shares and the third is 1,28,02,978 shares. APL Apollo said it is neither buyer nor seller under the agreement.

Tata Steel must then make an open offer for up to 7,28,06,387 shares, or 26% of the expanded voting capital, at ₹2,301.40 a share. CNBC reported that if the offer succeeds, Tata Steel would hold 52.38%. Business Standard put the second leg at around ₹32,267 crore.

In the first leg, Tata Steel will sell its steel tubes business and Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for ₹28,000 crore. APL Apollo's investor presentation says it expects to raise about ₹28,000 crore in debt, first through acquisition financing and later through long-term capitalisation. The presentation puts the deal at about 24.8 times projected FY27 Ebitda.

Bankers estimate annual interest of ₹2,800-3,900 crore on the loan, assuming borrowing costs of 10-14 per cent, Business Standard reported. APL Apollo reported Ebitda of ₹1,914 crore in FY26. Tata Steel's consolidated gross debt was ₹1.02 trillion at the end of September.
Tata Steel said the deal would lift its downstream integration to about 53% from 35%. T V Narendran, its chief executive, said it would "create a downstream powerhouse for the future".

Analysts were critical of the structure. Shriram Subramanian of InGovern Research Services said: "The transaction doesn't seem beneficial to either Tata Steel shareholders or APL Apollo minority shareholders." Deven Choksey of DRChoksey FinServ told CNBC the deal is likely positive in the long term but is "appearing very complex".

Amit Tandon of Institutional Investor Advisory Services India said institutional shareholders of neither company appear to get a vote under the Companies Act. Tata Steel scheduled an investor call after market hours on Monday.

stories.background: The agreement has two linked legs. APL Apollo acquires Tata Steel's steel tubes business and Tata Steel Colors using borrowed funds. Tata Steel then buys the promoters' stake in three tranches and makes an open offer to public shareholders. CNBC reported that ArcelorMittal was also reportedly interested in APL Apollo.
stories.whyItMatters: Shareholders of both companies saw share values fall, and APL Apollo would carry about ₹28,000 crore of new debt. That debt would show up in Tata Steel's consolidated borrowings if APL Apollo becomes a subsidiary.

stories.headline: FSSAI sanctions prosecution of Bisleri over water sample; company says it is safe
stories.dek: Bisleri says it has received no notice, that the sample dates to September 2025, and that independent testing found bromate within limits.
stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India said on Sunday it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a water sample was declared unsafe. Bisleri said on Monday its water is safe and it has received no notice.
body: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said on Sunday, November 22, that it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a packaged drinking water sample from the company's premises was declared unsafe in laboratory tests.

The regulator said the sample was non-compliant with prescribed bromate limits and was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. After the company appealed, it said, the referral food laboratory also declared the sample unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).

In a statement, the FSSAI said an order prohibiting sale was issued for Batch No. Go 270. "Only one batch was found to be non-compliant," it said, adding that the company had been asked to conduct a root cause analysis. It also said that, under the law, the referral lab's report is final when a food business operator appeals.

Bisleri said on Monday that its packaged drinking water was safe for consumption. It said it had received no notice by email or in hard copy and could not locate the reported notice on the FSSAI website.

The company said the matter concerned a batch made in September 2025 at its Goa plant, one of 143 in its network. According to Bisleri, the FSSAI collected six samples on September 30, 2025. Five met standards, while the sixth showed bromate at 12 micrograms per litre against a limit of 10.

Bisleri said it appealed on November 22, 2025. The referral laboratory then found bromate within the limit but flagged PAHs, the company said. It said it had the same sample tested at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which also found bromate within limits.

The company said it sent those results to the FSSAI's Western Regional Office in a letter dated February 2, 2026, and heard nothing further. It said it understood the matter to be closed. A spokesperson told The Hindu that management was deciding on next steps.
"Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri," the company said, citing over 90 tests across a 10-step manufacturing process. It said it would continue to cooperate with the FSSAI.

NDTV, citing sources, reported that the FSSAI has also sampled other major packaged water brands and inspected facilities, and is expected to take legal action against companies found in violation. The regulator's prosecution sanction is not a judicial finding of guilt.
keyFacts: FSSAI announced the prosecution sanction against Bisleri International on Sunday, November 22, 2026.
Bisleri says the sample came from a September 2025 batch at its Goa plant.

FSSAI says the referral lab detected PAHs; Bisleri says that lab found bromate within limits.
Bisleri says it has received no formal notice of the action.
stories.background: Bromate can form when ozone used to disinfect water reacts with naturally occurring bromide. The WHO has a provisional guideline value of 10 micrograms per litre, and the IARC classes bromate as possibly carcinogenic to humans. PAHs are a group of compounds, some of which are classed as carcinogenic.
stories.whyItMatters: The prosecution sanction affects one of India's best-known packaged water brands, and reported FSSAI sampling of other brands could extend scrutiny across the sector.

stories.headline: Supreme Court says it may allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not all NCR
stories.dek: The bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant also proposed a five-year plan to move goods unloading to border warehouses and keep commercial vehicles out of the capital.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court said on Monday it may allow only BS-VI-compliant vehicles in Delhi, if not the wider NCR, and floated a five-year plan on commercial vehicles. The Week reported Delhi's AQI rose to 260, with 'very poor' air likely by November 26.
body: The Supreme Court on Monday said it may allow only vehicles meeting Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission standards to operate in Delhi, as it heard a matter on air pollution in Delhi-NCR.

The bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the remarks. News agency ANI quoted the bench as saying: "We are clear we will allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not NCR."

The court also proposed a five-year plan to eventually keep commercial vehicles out of the capital. Under the idea, goods would be unloaded at warehouses on Delhi's borders and brought into the city on battery-operated or other non-polluting vehicles, The Times of India reported.

The bench said essential items would still have to reach residents. "They require vegetables, they require fruits, they need other day-to-day items, daily items. So everything will have to be available. So what can be the alternative?" it asked.

The CJI asked whether border warehousing could allow cleaner vehicles to carry goods into the city. The bench clarified that the proposal may not be practical immediately but could be developed over the next five years as a long-term measure to reduce vehicular emissions.
The court is hearing suo motu proceedings on air pollution in Delhi-NCR. The case covers several sources, including firecrackers, crop residue burning and solid waste management.
Separately, The Week reported that Delhi's air quality index rose to 260 on Monday and was likely to worsen to the 'very poor' category by November 26.

stories.whyItMatters: Any restriction to BS-VI vehicles or on commercial vehicles would affect transporters and vehicle owners in Delhi, and the supply of daily goods to residents.

stories.headline: ICMR survey finds lower anaemia prevalence than earlier national surveys
stories.dek: The SAMPADA survey reports severe anaemia in under 2% of most age groups, with about half of anaemic women and children having mild cases.
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research released its SAMPADA 2023-2025 survey on Monday, reporting lower anaemia prevalence than earlier national surveys. Severe anaemia affected less than 2% of people in most age groups, and iron deficiency explained about half of cases.
body: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) released a national survey on Monday, November 23, reporting lower anaemia prevalence across age groups than previous national surveys, with severe anaemia seen in less than 2% of people in most age groups.

The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025 covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin.

Prevalence was 42% among children aged 12-59 months and 46% among adolescent girls aged 10-19 years. Women of reproductive age had a prevalence of 56%. Adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20-59 years had 22-23%.

The report said about half of anaemic women, including pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls and children have mild anaemia, which it described as carrying a considerably lower risk of serious health consequences than moderate or severe forms. Among anaemic boys and men, three-fourths have only mild anaemia, according to a Union Health Ministry release.

Iron deficiency accounts for about half of anaemia cases in women, adolescent girls and children, the report said. It is largely restricted to under-five children, adolescent girls and women of reproductive age, and is common among people with moderate and severe anaemia. The report said other causes, including infections, haemoglobinopathies and inflammation linked to chronic disease, also need to be addressed.
Vitamin B12 and folate deficiency was similar in anaemic and non-anaemic people, indicating a limited contribution to anaemia in India, the report said.

The survey used venous blood sampling and automated analysers for haemoglobin estimation. In a sub-sample it also assessed iron, folate, vitamin B12 and the inflammatory markers C-reactive protein and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein.

Rajiv Bahl, secretary of the Department of Health Research, said: "It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys." He said the findings give an evidence base for the ongoing Anaemia Mukt Bharat efforts.

Bharati Kulkarni, director of ICMR-NIN, said the findings support "more targeted, population-specific and life-course approaches to anaemia prevention and management." The release said people with moderate and severe anaemia need testing, treatment and tracking until resolution, as envisaged in Anaemia Mukt Bharat 2.0.
keyFacts: SAMPADA 2023-2025 was released on Monday, November 23, 2026.
Survey covered over 2 lakh people in 183 districts across 35 States and UTs.

stories.background: Anaemia Mukt Bharat is the national programme to reduce anaemia. The survey report refers to its second phase, AMB 2.0, in describing how moderate and severe cases should be identified and treated.
stories.whyItMatters: The findings point to iron deficiency concentrated in children, adolescent girls and women of reproductive age, which the report says supports targeted prevention and treatment under Anaemia Mukt Bharat.

stories.headline: Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma submits resignation over elephant drive; Forest Dept halts operation
stories.dek: The Congress legislator said the department moved elephants into her constituency without consulting her; the Speaker's office has received the letter but has not accepted it.
stories.summary: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation to the Speaker's office in Bengaluru on Monday, objecting to an operation that pushed elephants from Hassan into Mudigere. The Forest Department stopped the drive that day, and Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy called a meeting for November 30.
body: Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma of the Congress submitted her resignation letter at the Karnataka Legislative Assembly Speaker's office in Bengaluru on Monday, protesting a Forest Department operation that drove wild elephants from Hassan district towards Chikkamagaluru district.

An official told The Indian Express that the office had received the letter but not yet accepted it. The Hindu reported that the Speaker was away and that Motamma asked officials to accept it. Reporters pointed out the letter was not in the proper format, and she said she would submit another if needed.

In her letter, Motamma said she was resigning "with pain and disappointment" because the department decided to drive the elephants to the Tatkola Reserve Forest, within her constituency, without consulting her, according to The Hindu. At a press conference in Chikkamagaluru on Sunday, she had said she would resign if the elephants were not withdrawn within a day.

The operation began after two people died in Belur taluk of Hassan within three days last week. The department used 12 kumkis, or tamed elephants, with over 350 staff and more than 100 police personnel. Officials first captured two tuskers said to be responsible for the deaths and moved them to Nagarahole.

Hassan district in-charge minister K M Shivalinge Gowda ordered the herds driven towards Bhadra. He said there was no forest cover in Hassan. "There is enough forest area in Bhadra wildlife," he said. He added that if the elephants got stuck in Chikkamagaluru, he would stand by its people and join their protests.

On Monday, Chikkamagaluru Deputy Conservator of Forests K T Boraiah said senior officers had directed that no drive be carried out that day. By then 38 elephants had entered Mudigere taluk, in two groups 2-3 km apart, at Baradahalli and Makonahalli. About 60-70 personnel and drones were monitoring them. Schools nearby were given a holiday.
Boraiah said there would be no driving for now, as the coffee harvest is under way. He asked the public not to burst crackers or go out to film the animals.
Residents gathered in Mudigere town on Monday to demand the elephants be withdrawn. Former MLC M K Pranesh said the taluk would call a bandh if the government did not respond.

BJP MLC C T Ravi, a former minister, told reporters in Chikkamagaluru that MLAs should stop the "drama" of announcing resignations. He said he knew "nobody will resign" and that the ruling party's MLAs should instead demand the resignation of the minister who ordered the operation.

Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy has convened a meeting of elected representatives and senior forest officials in Bengaluru on November 30 to discuss the herds' movement, public safety and ways to prevent repeated human-elephant conflict.
keyFacts: Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation to the Speaker's office on Monday; it has not been accepted.

stories.background:
Wild elephants have been reported in parts of Hassan since the 1980s. According to earlier reports cited by The Hindu, 24 people have died in elephant attacks in the district since 2020-21. Officials say Hassan has no forest comparable to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary.

Motamma was first elected from the Scheduled Caste-reserved Mudigere seat in 2023.
stories.whyItMatters: Residents of Mudigere and neighbouring taluks face elephants near homes and coffee estates during the harvest, while Hassan villagers have faced deaths and crop losses.

stories.headline: Namma Metro ridership up 12%, but net loss widens to ₹1,710 crore
stories.dek: BMRCL's finance costs rose to ₹1,793.03 crore in 2025–26 from ₹560.01 crore a year earlier, even as fare revenue grew 49%.
stories.summary: BMRCL's annual report for 2025–26 shows ridership up 12.29% and fare revenue up 49.36% to ₹1,125.58 crore. A sharp rise in finance costs still widened its net loss to ₹1,710.13 crore.
body: The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) reported a net loss of ₹1,710.13 crore for 2025–26, up from ₹1,405.67 crore the previous year, according to its 20th annual report, even as ridership and fare revenue rose sharply.
Finance cost climbed to ₹1,793.03 crore from ₹560.01 crore in 2024–25. Depreciation was ₹725.36 crore, against ₹576.79 crore a year earlier. The report puts the loss before tax at ₹1,717.46 crore.

Passenger journeys totalled 310.49 million, compared with 276.51 million in 2024–25, a rise of 12.29%. Average daily ridership increased to 8.51 lakh from 7.57 lakh. The highest single-day ridership, 10.82 lakh, came on August 14, 2025, when fare revenue hit a record ₹4.58 crore.

Fare-box revenue rose 49.36% to ₹1,125.58 crore from ₹753.59 crore. Non-fare revenue grew 61.02% to ₹88.51 crore from ₹54.97 crore. BMRCL attributed the fare growth mainly to higher ridership after the 19.15-km Yellow Line between RV Road and Bommasandra opened in August 2025.

Gross income rose about 46.2% to ₹1,624.62 crore from ₹1,111.59 crore. Operating expenditure was ₹823.69 crore, against ₹665.50 crore. Profit before interest and depreciation was ₹800.93 crore, up from ₹446.09 crore. The corporation reported an operational profit of ₹417.42 crore and a cash profit of ₹209.66 crore.

BMRCL has not recommended a dividend for the year. Trains ran with 99.85% punctuality, the report said. Its paid-up share capital was ₹15,987.72 crore on March 31, 2026, and authorised capital was raised from ₹16,000 crore to ₹22,000 crore after shareholders approved the change in September 2025.

Separately, The Times of India reported that two flyovers are proposed parallel to the Green Line on Kanakapura Road, flanking the Metro corridor, to ease traffic at the Kanakapura Road–Vasanthapura Road and Konanakunte Cross junctions. The junctions are about 125 metres apart and together handle over 2.7 lakh vehicles a day, according to a survey on April 2, 2025.

The detailed project report puts the cost at Rs 291 crore, of which Rs 191.3 crore is for land and structure acquisition. It identifies 6,848 sqm of private land for acquisition through Transfer of Development Rights, but does not say how many properties or owners are affected.
Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said: "The tendering process has been completed and work will begin once we receive govt approval."

Fare-box revenue grew 49.36% to ₹1,125.58 crore.

stories.background: BMRCL is undertaking Phase 2, Phase 2A, Phase 2B and Phase 3 expansion projects, involving spending on infrastructure, land acquisition, construction and rolling stock. The Yellow Line between RV Road and Bommasandra opened in August 2025.
stories.whyItMatters: The figures show Metro ridership and fare income growing while borrowing costs for network expansion keep BMRCL loss-making. The proposed flyovers would affect traffic on Kanakapura Road and require private land through Transfer of Development Rights.

stories.headline: Karnataka forest department proposes 10 green spaces around Bengaluru, to go to Cabinet
stories.dek: Both reports say the plan is expected before the Cabinet on November 30, with entry tickets funding upkeep and CSR money backing the works.
stories.summary: The Karnataka forest department has proposed ten green spaces or tree parks in and around Bengaluru, to be placed before the Cabinet on November 30. The Times of India and The Hindu report different acreage and cost figures.
body: The Karnataka forest department has drawn up a plan for ten large green spaces and tree parks in and around Bengaluru, which is expected to go before the State Cabinet on November 30, according to The Times of India and The Hindu.

The two outlets report different figures. The Times of India put the plan at 3,453 acres and Rs 150 crore, funded mainly through corporate social responsibility (CSR) and corporate environmental responsibility (CER) funds. The Hindu, citing the proposal, reported 3,271 acres across nine locations at an indicative cost of ₹222 crore, with funding in phases from 2026-27 through State Budget allocations and CSR funds.

The Times of India said entry to all ten sites would cost Rs 10 per person, with gate collections used for daily maintenance. A forest department official told the paper that no decision had been taken on allowing commercial activity such as food stalls. The Hindu reported that the proposal says ticket revenue would be retained for maintaining each park.

Only part of the land would be opened to visitors. The Times of India said 2,281 of the 3,453 acres would remain protected forest and 1,172 acres would be accessible. At Turahalli minor forest, 78 acres would be opened and 519 acres would be an eco-protected zone. The Hindu reported that 1,303 acres would be open to the public and 1,968 acres set aside for ecological restoration and conservation.

The sites named include two forest blocks at Turahalli, the Kalkere forest ecology centre inside Bannerghatta National Park, the Doresanipalya research and extension centre, Marasandra, Mandur, Panathur and Jarakabande. The Times of India also listed Bannerghatta National Park itself.

Jarakabande gets the largest allocation. The Times of India gave it Rs 35.6 crore. The Hindu said the Jarakabande Tree Cultivation Centre in A Block has over ₹35 crore, followed by Kalkere at ₹21.91 crore, and more than ₹16 crore each for the two Turahalli projects.

Planned features include walking, trekking and cycling trails, seating, nature walks, information panels, thematic tree plantations, medicinal plant gardens and spaces for environmental education. The Hindu reported that the plan would replace eucalyptus and acacia plantations with indigenous species, but only after work plans are approved. It also lists restored ponds at Turahalli, a bamboo collection at Mandur and an expanded biodiversity park at Panathur.

Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy told The Hindu that Bengaluru, with a population of over one crore, lacks enough parks and green spaces. He said the department hopes to finish all the work within a year, and that several organisations had expressed interest in supporting it. The Times of India quoted him as saying: "We intend to cash in on the potential of environmental tourism."
After in-principle approval, the department will prepare Detailed Project Reports for each location and seek administrative approval with the Finance Department's concurrence, The Hindu reported.
keyFacts: The proposal is expected before the State Cabinet on November 30.

Minister Ramalinga Reddy said work is meant to finish within a year.
stories.background:
The Hindu reported that the proposal follows several months of land inspection and identification after D.K. Shivakumar became Chief Minister. Officials had earlier said they wanted spaces on the lines of Cubbon Park and Lalbagh.

The 154-acre Madappanahalli biodiversity park in North Bengaluru, listed in the proposal, received Cabinet approval in January with initial funding of ₹50 crore, The Hindu reported.
stories.whyItMatters: If approved, residents would get new ticketed green spaces with trails, while eucalyptus and acacia plantations at the sites would be replaced with indigenous trees.

stories.headline: New Zealand bat out 120 overs to draw first Test against India in Wellington
stories.dek: Shubman Gill called the Basin Reserve surface "not a great Test wicket" after India, who declared on 720 for 9, took only five second-innings wickets.
stories.summary: New Zealand finished on 239 for five after India needed eight wickets on the final day at the Basin Reserve, and the captains shook hands with 15 overs left. India captain Shubman Gill criticised the pitch after the draw.
body: New Zealand batted out the final day at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Monday to draw the first Test against India, finishing their second innings on 239 for five after India began the day needing eight wickets.
The captains shook hands with 15 of the scheduled overs unbowled. New Zealand still trailed India's first-innings 720 for 9 declared by 113 runs. The hosts made 368 in their first innings.

Washington Sundar, Prasidh Krishna and Anshul Kamboj took the three wickets of the day. Washington had Devon Conway caught by Rishabh Pant off bat and pad for 65. Prasidh removed Rachin Ravindra for 37, caught by KL Rahul at second slip. Kamboj then had Tom Blundell caught behind for 15, confirmed on review, to leave New Zealand 176 for five.

Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips then batted 43 overs together, adding 63. Mitchell was unbeaten on 49 from 186 balls and Phillips on 26 from 126. ESPNcricinfo reported eight consecutive maidens before tea and 43 consecutive dot balls after it.

India missed chances. Akash Deep fumbled at mid-on and let go a run-out opportunity against Mitchell, and Devdutt Padikkal could not hold a catch at forward short leg off Mitchell's glove. ESPNcricinfo noted that India had no short leg when Prasidh drew an earlier bat-pad chance from Mitchell.

Gill criticised the surface afterwards. "On Day(s) 3, 4, and 5, it just went flatter and flatter," he said. "The wicket just got slower, so having seen that, I think it was not a great Test wicket, especially if you want results." He also said: "We knew it was going to be a challenge to get 10 wickets on that pitch."
The Indian Express reported more than 1,300 runs for 24 wickets over the five days. ESPNcricinfo said only 91 false shots were created in the final innings, against 99 and 96 in the first two.
New Zealand's Henry Nicholls, who made an unbeaten 175 in the first innings, said: "For us to get a draw from where we were was a pleasing result."
The second Test starts in Christchurch on Friday.
keyFacts: India 720 for 9 declared; New Zealand 368 and 239 for 5.
Mitchell finished on 49 not out from 186 balls; Phillips on 26 from 126.
Prasidh Krishna took 2 for 23 in 19 overs.
India remain fourth in the World Test Championship table; New Zealand are third.
Second Test starts in Christchurch on Friday.
stories.background: New Zealand were 70 for five on the opening day before a sixth-wicket stand of 216 between Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips lifted them to 368. India's innings included centuries from KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant, and Gill fell two runs short of one. Jasprit Bumrah was playing his first Test in a year.

stories.headline: Adani Airports raises ₹2,790 crore from 360 ONE Asset in equity deal
stories.dek: The fresh $300 million takes the airport unit's total equity fundraising to $1.35 billion, after an earlier $1 billion round from Temasek, Premji Invest and others.
stories.summary: Adani Airport Holdings has signed a binding agreement to raise ₹2,790 crore ($300 million) from 360 ONE Asset. Together with an earlier $1 billion round, the investors will hold about 7.01% of the company.
body: Adani Airport Holdings Ltd (AAHL), a subsidiary of Adani Enterprises Ltd, has signed a binding agreement to raise ₹2,790 crore ($300 million) from 360 ONE Alternates Asset Management Ltd, taking its total equity fundraising to $1.35 billion.

360 ONE, acting through its funds and affiliates, will subscribe to newly issued AAHL shares on the same terms and valuation as the earlier investors. It has also joined the shareholders' agreement signed with them, the company said.

The earlier round raised ₹9,825 crore ($1 billion) in primary equity from a consortium that included Alpha Wave Global, Premji Invest, Temasek and funds managed by BlackRock. According to a company statement cited by NDTV, the two rounds value AAHL at about $18 billion on a pre-money basis.
Once both transactions are complete, the investors will together hold about 7.01% of AAHL. The deal is subject to customary conditions, including applicable approvals, the company said.

AAHL said the money would go towards three priorities: modernising and upgrading its existing airports, developing integrated airport cities, and expanding passenger-facing and other non-aeronautical businesses.

The company aims to raise annual passenger-handling capacity from about 96 million to 200 million. It runs eight airports: Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Jaipur, Guwahati, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram. They handled about 95.3 million passengers in FY26, according to its investor presentation, or about 23% of India's passenger traffic.

Jeet Adani, non-executive director of AAHL, said: "This partnership is yet another milestone in building out the Adani Airports platform." He added that the company was committed to turning airports "from simple transit hubs into vibrant airport cities that merge aviation, commerce, leisure, and regional logistics".
Government data show India's aviation market handled about 420 million passengers in FY26. The country's airports have a combined annual capacity of more than 580 million.

stories.headline: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok's sexualised deepfakes and safety claims
stories.dek: The attorneys general say SpaceX, which now owns xAI, failed to stop Grok and X users creating child sexual abuse material and misled consumers about safety.
stories.summary: Oregon and Virginia filed separate state-court lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging its Grok AI tool and the X platform enabled sexualised deepfakes, including of children. SpaceX says people who bypass its safeguards should be prosecuted.
body: Oregon and Virginia have sued Elon Musk's SpaceX in state courts, alleging that its Grok AI image generator and the social network X allowed users to create and share sexualised deepfakes, including child sexual abuse material.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed his complaint in Multnomah County Circuit Court on Sunday evening. Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones filed in the City of Richmond Circuit Court on Monday morning. CNBC reported that, as of early Monday, both suits were awaiting the courts' acceptance.

CNBC described the two as the first states to sue the company over Grok. The complaints also allege that SpaceX falsely presented Grok and X as generally safe, which the states say breaches Virginia's Consumer Protection Act and Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. Both states are seeking injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs. Virginia also wants restitution for consumers.

The Verge reported that the complaints centre on Grok Imagine, a tool that generates images and videos. The Virginia complaint accuses Musk of ignoring concerns about AI-generated sexualised deepfakes and seeing "a market opportunity for more profits". It calls the weak safeguards "not a failure but a feature".

"Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false," Jones said in a press statement. Rayfield wrote that such conduct "erodes important norms regarding consent and privacy and trivializes sexual imagery, abuse, and exploitation."

SpaceX, which owns xAI, said in a statement posted on X's Safety account that it takes action against people who try to break its safeguards, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement. It said those who attempt to create such material should be prosecuted "to the fullest extent of the law".

The X Safety team said people who generated the material had deliberately violated its terms of service and worked to circumvent safeguards. It said it tightened Grok Imagine's protections after some users found ways to misuse it earlier this year, and that classifiers screen every prompt and check every output.

The Verge said its own testing after xAI restricted image editing found the changes did little to stop sexualised deepfakes. CNBC cited research by the Internet Watch Foundation and the Center for Countering Digital Hate on the tools' use to make explicit images from real photos.

SpaceX already faces Grok-related lawsuits and government investigations in the U.K., Spain, Ireland, France and California, CNBC reported. In a suit by the city of Baltimore, the company argued that Section 230 shields it from liability for users' content.
keyFacts: Oregon filed on Sunday evening in Multnomah County Circuit Court; Virginia filed on Monday in Richmond.

stories.background:
xAI launched a "spicy" mode for Grok Imagine in August 2025, according to The Verge, and Musk has since merged xAI with SpaceX. In January 2026, Grok gained a feature letting X users edit any image without the original poster's consent, and the platform was flooded with nonconsensual sexualised deepfakes of adults and minors, The Verge reported.

State attorneys general have won changes from tech firms before. In August, Meta settled a federal case over claims it misrepresented harms to children's mental health, agreeing without admitting wrongdoing to pay states around $17 billion over 10 years, CNBC reported.
stories.whyItMatters: The suits could lead to court orders restricting how Grok and X operate and to financial penalties. Virginia is also seeking restitution for consumers.

stories.headline: Amazon agrees to buy Decart's chip software and hire its founders
stories.dek: The Israeli startup's software helps AI models run across Nvidia, Amazon and Google chips; Bloomberg put the price at about $7.5 billion, which Amazon did not confirm.
stories.summary: Amazon said on Monday it will buy the technology of Israeli AI startup Decart and hire its founders and researchers. Bloomberg reported the price at about $7.5 billion; Amazon declined to comment on the terms.
body: Amazon said on Monday it has agreed to buy the proprietary technology of Israeli AI startup Decart and to hire its three founders, along with its AI researchers and engineers.

Amazon declined to disclose the financial terms. Bloomberg News reported the value at about $7.5 billion, citing people familiar with the matter. Decart did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The core of the deal is the Decart Optimization Stack, or DOS, a software engine that helps companies run AI systems efficiently and switch between chips from Nvidia, Amazon and Google. Decart, founded in 2023, also builds real-time world models, the latest being Oasis 3, and AI video generation tools. Its CEO is Dean Leitersdorf.

Amazon said it has worked with Decart since 2025 to improve performance on its Trainium chips. It said the technology will help it optimise inference and custom silicon so customers can train and run AI models faster and at lower cost.

"Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip," said Peter DeSantis, a senior vice president at Amazon who oversees foundation models, custom silicon and quantum computing. "More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost."

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said last month the company plans to offer Trainium chips externally for the first time "late in 2027". Amazon has so far used them in its own data centres. TechCrunch reported that Decart's software could make it easier for customers to run workloads on Amazon chips rather than on Nvidia's.

The reported price would be a large jump from Decart's most recent valuation of nearly $4 billion, according to PitchBook data. In May, Decart raised $300 million in a round led by Radical Ventures, with Nvidia joining as a new investor. Bloomberg reported in September that Anthropic had explored buying Decart but decided against it after due diligence.

The deal is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory clearance. Structures in which a company hires a startup's founders and licenses or buys its technology without acquiring the whole company have drawn regulatory scrutiny in some cases, CNBC reported.

stories.background: Big technology companies have struck a series of deals to license AI startups' technology or hire their founders. Amazon made two similar deals in 2024, with Adept and Covariant. Meta bought a 49 per cent stake in Scale AI for $14.3 billion last year, and AMD agreed in September to buy World Labs for $8.2 billion.
stories.whyItMatters: Amazon is preparing to sell Trainium chips to outside customers in competition with Nvidia, the dominant supplier, and software that eases switching between chips could affect how easily customers move.

stories.headline: Pakistani astronaut to fly to China's Tiangong station on Shenzhou-24
stories.dek: The payload specialist would be the first foreign national to visit the station; the astronaut's name and the launch date have not been announced.
stories.summary: China's Manned Space Agency has selected a Pakistani astronaut to join the Shenzhou-24 mission to the Tiangong space station, according to Al Jazeera citing Chinese state media. A US space entrepreneur told NDTV the flight is also a geopolitical signal.
body: China's Manned Space Agency has selected a Pakistani astronaut to fly as a payload specialist on the Shenzhou-24 mission to the Tiangong space station, making the person the first foreign national to visit it, according to Al Jazeera, which cited Chinese state media.
The astronaut's identity and the departure date have not been announced. The mission is expected to take place before the end of the year, The Indian Express reported.

Pakistani pilots Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud were among the candidates who trained for months at the China Astronaut Research and Training Center in Beijing. The training followed an agreement the two countries signed in February 2025 to set up a programme for selecting and preparing Pakistani astronauts. It included operational exercises and intensive Chinese language lessons.
The astronaut will conduct scientific experiments in microgravity aboard the station, NDTV reported. It will be the first time China's crewed programme carries a foreign astronaut.

George Weinmann, an American space entrepreneur and founder of Hab Space, said the mission reflects the growing maturity of China's human spaceflight programme. Speaking to NDTV in New Delhi, where he is attending the India International Space Conclave 2026, he said China had been signalling for years that it wanted its station to be a platform for international cooperation.
"On the other hand, of course, it is also a geopolitical signal that China is becoming more internationally active with other countries," Weinmann said.

He linked the interest in Tiangong to the approaching retirement of the International Space Station. NASA plans to be a customer of privately owned stations in low Earth orbit rather than an owner, which he said leaves other countries wondering what to do. He added that US legislation continues to limit direct cooperation with China's space programme.

The Indian Express noted that the cooperation extends beyond crewed flight. China's National Space Administration is set to deploy Jinnah-1, Pakistan's first lunar rover, which weighs 35 kg and carries instruments to study plasma behaviour, radiation levels and the composition of lunar soil.
Weinmann said India, which is preparing its Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme, should see the mission as encouraging. "We should not rest on our heels," he said.

Pakistan's Jinnah-1 lunar rover weighs 35 kg and will be deployed by China.
stories.background: China has expanded its space programme in recent years and has set a target of landing astronauts on the Moon by 2030. Pakistan and China have long-standing strategic and diplomatic ties, and China is Pakistan's largest trading partner and a key foreign investor, The Indian Express reported.
stories.whyItMatters: The flight would open China's station to a foreign astronaut for the first time, at a point when the International Space Station is nearing the end of its service.

stories.headline: NASA invites industry bids to design Lunar Reactor-1 fission power system
stories.dek: The 20-kilowatt reactor is meant to run for at least five years on the Moon, including through its roughly two-week nights, with proposals due by Dec. 21.
stories.summary: NASA has issued a request for proposals seeking industry partners to develop and test Lunar Reactor-1, a small fission power system for the Moon. The agency aims to have it launch-ready by 2030.
body: NASA has asked industry to propose designs for Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1), a small fission power system intended to supply electricity on the Moon, according to an agency announcement on Monday. Proposals are due by Dec. 21.

LR-1 is planned to generate 20 kilowatts of electricity. NASA said that is enough to power about 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For the agency's Moon Base plans, it could support habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments and other infrastructure.
NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and to operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment.

The agency said a reactor, unlike solar power, can produce electricity continuously, including through lunar nights that last about 14 Earth days. That would help operations in places where sunlight is limited or absent.

"This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface," said Brian Giblin, NASA's Lunar Reactor-1 program manager.

The solicitation, titled the Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals, reflects feedback on a draft released in August and an industry day held in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. It requires the reactor to meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations.
The main purpose is to advance the technology, testing and flight design of LR-1. NASA said it may also issue further task orders for other space nuclear power systems.

LR-1 is managed by NASA's Space Reactors Division in partnership with the DOE. The same division is responsible for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, scheduled to launch in 2028. That mission is to deliver three SkyFall helicopters to Mars and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion, in which a reactor's electricity powers a spacecraft's propulsion systems.

NASA says lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months, and solar power becomes less effective farther from the Sun.
stories.whyItMatters: NASA says a continuous power source is needed for sustained operations on the lunar surface, including where sunlight is limited, and for later exploration of Mars.

stories.headline: CMC Vellore and TIFR unveil India's first human metabolic chamber
stories.dek: Volunteers will live inside the airtight room for a full day or more while scientists measure how their bodies burn fuel, to study diabetes and obesity.
stories.summary: CMC Vellore and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research unveiled India's first human metabolic chamber on Monday. The room measures energy use over a full daily cycle, which researchers say will help study diabetes, obesity and malnutrition in Indian populations.
body: The Christian Medical College (CMC) in Vellore and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) on Monday unveiled what they described as India's first Human Metabolic Chamber, a room in which volunteers live while scientists measure how their bodies use energy.

The chamber was set up jointly by CMC and TIFR's Metabolism, Development and Aging (ARUMDA) programme. Punya Salila Srivastava, secretary in the Union health and family welfare ministry, inaugurated it.

The airtight room has a bed, a desk and a toilet, and is laid out like a hotel room. Meals are passed in through an airlock, and volunteers work, rest, eat and sleep inside while researchers monitor them.

Scientists call the device a whole-room indirect calorimeter. They measure oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide output to calculate the energy burned during sleep, rest, digestion and physical activity. The data also show how the body switches between fat and carbohydrate across meals, activity and sleep, and how it responds to a given diet, medicine or sleep pattern.

Most metabolic tests capture a snapshot of 20 to 30 minutes, often through a face mask. The chamber follows a person through a whole day under controlled conditions. “This lets it detect small but important differences between individuals that shorter tests miss,” said Dr Nihal Thomas, senior professor of endocrinology, diabetes and metabolism at CMC Vellore.

Ullas Kolthur-Seetharam, ARUMDA coordinator and principal investigator, said Indians are under-represented in global metabolic research. He said the chamber will help show how energy use varies across India's populations, diets and lifestyles, and will inform nutritional interventions.

It will also support long-term studies, including a Vellore birth cohort that CMC has followed since 2010–12. A joint ARUMDA–CMC study of the cohort, published in 2026 in The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia, found overweight and obesity nearly tripled between ages seven and nine, while about one in five children remained thin.

Researchers said the chamber can be combined with ARUMDA's National Analytical Facility for Nutrition and Metabolism Research, which offers metabolomics, body-composition and stable-isotope methods. That would let them link energy use to what is happening in blood and tissues.

The facility is funded by the department of atomic energy and by CSR support from Hindustan Unilever Limited. NUTRIM at Maastricht University provided expert advice, and the Embassy of the Kingdom of Netherlands in India gave network support. The cost of building the chamber was not disclosed.

Research will focus on obesity, diabetes, ageing, malnutrition and cancer care. The team said precise data on energy needs could strengthen the evidence behind programmes such as POSHAN Abhiyaan and Anaemia Mukt Bharat.
keyFacts: The chamber was unveiled at CMC Vellore on Monday.
It was built by CMC and TIFR's ARUMDA programme.
Standard metabolic tests last 20 to 30 minutes; the chamber measures a full day.
Funding came from the department of atomic energy and Hindustan Unilever Limited CSR support.
The construction cost was not disclosed.
stories.background: The research team said the chamber builds on India's calorimetry tradition, including work at St John's Medical College, Bangalore, from the late 1980s. Researchers also point to India's double burden of malnutrition, in which undernutrition and obesity exist in the same communities and even among children.
stories.whyItMatters: Researchers say the data could explain why people of similar body weight differ in diabetes and heart disease risk, and support diet advice suited to Indian foods and lifestyles.

stories.headline: FIFA awards 2031 Women's World Cup to US-led bid, 2035 edition to UK
stories.dek: Both bids were unopposed. The 2035 tournament will be the first World Cup held in the United Kingdom since the men's event in 1966.
stories.summary: FIFA's Extraordinary Congress on Monday approved the joint bid by the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for 2031, and the UK's bid for 2035. The 2031 edition will be the first Women's World Cup with 48 teams.
body: FIFA confirmed on Monday that the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup, and that England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will host the 2035 edition.

The decisions were taken at a special FIFA Congress held virtually from its Zurich headquarters. Both bids were unopposed and approved by acclamation, CNA reported. FIFA had limited eligibility for 2031 to associations from Africa and CONCACAF, and for 2035 to associations from Africa and Europe.

The 2031 tournament will be the first Women's World Cup co-hosted by four nations and the first with 48 teams. It will be the third in North America, after the US hosted in 1999 and 2003 and Canada in 2015. The 2035 edition will keep the 48-team format, with 12 groups of four and a knockout round starting at the last 32.

US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone said: "Together with FIFA, we are committed to delivering a world-class tournament and will use this historic opportunity to accelerate the growth of women's football around the world." Emily Cosler, US Soccer's vice-president of strategy, told The Guardian the federation expects the event to be "the largest women's sporting event in history".

The 2035 tournament will be the first World Cup of any kind in the United Kingdom since the men's event in 1966, BBC News reported. The 'All Together' bid proposes 104 matches over 39 days at 19 venues: 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales. Three more grounds could be added, taking the total to 22 venues in 16 cities.

Debbie Hewitt, chair of the English Football Association, said: "We want this to be your Women's World Cup, a World Cup for everyone." British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the tournament would bring "visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country".

FIFA's evaluation of the UK bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five and its contractual framework "medium risk". It said certain government guarantees, particularly on tax and safety and security, contained qualifications. BBC News said this is thought to refer to a FIFA request for tax-free status for football-related activities. FIFA has not yet decided whether all four host nations will qualify automatically.
The next Women's World Cup, the 10th, will be held in Brazil from June 24 to July 25, 2027.
keyFacts: FIFA approved both bids by acclamation at its Extraordinary Congress on Monday.
The 2031 hosts are the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica.
The 2035 tournament will be the UK's first World Cup since 1966.
Both tournaments will feature 48 teams.
The 2027 Women's World Cup runs from June 24 to July 25 in Brazil.
stories.background: The US hosted the Women's World Cup in 1999 and 2003 and has won it four times. England staged the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won. England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will co-host the men's European Championship in 2028.
stories.whyItMatters: The UK government announced a vision for one million more girls to play, watch or take leadership roles in sport by the time of the 2035 tournament. BBC News reported that women hold only a quarter of chief executive, chair or performance director roles in major UK sports.

stories.headline: Marc Marquez wins eighth MotoGP title, equalling Giacomo Agostini's record
stories.dek: The Ducati rider overcame a 102-point deficit, the largest in MotoGP history, and clinched the championship with one race weekend still to run in Valencia.
stories.summary: Marc Marquez secured his eighth premier-class MotoGP title at the Portuguese Grand Prix in Portimao on Sunday, level with Giacomo Agostini. He recovered from a 102-point deficit after a crash and surgeries earlier in the season.
body: Marc Marquez won the 2026 MotoGP world championship at the Portuguese Grand Prix in Portimao on Sunday, taking his eighth premier-class title and equalling the record held by Italy's Giacomo Agostini.

The 33-year-old Spaniard, riding for the factory Ducati team, clinched the crown with one race weekend left, in Valencia. He had missed two earlier chances to seal it, in Qatar and in Saturday's sprint race in the Algarve, BBC Sport reported.

Marquez overcame the biggest points deficit in MotoGP history, 102 points, to win. He fell behind after a crash in the sprint race at Le Mans in May, which required operations on his foot and shoulder and kept him out of the next round in Barcelona. He returned at Mugello 20 days later, with Marco Bezzecchi leading the standings. He then won seven of the next 13 grands prix.
Marquez described the low point to BBC Sport on Monday. "In that moment after the crash in Le Mans and then the seventh surgery on the right shoulder, [my title charge] was completely over," he said.

Agostini, now 84, surprised Marquez on stage in Portugal and presented him with a golden helmet. Marquez said: "It is a big pleasure to equal Giacomo Agostini in premier class titles. He is the greatest of all time."

At 33 years and 278 days, Marquez is the oldest MotoGP champion of the modern era. The title is his 10th world championship, counting wins in the 125cc and Moto2 classes. That is one more than Valentino Rossi, who has nine.

Asked about the debate over the sport's greatest rider, Marquez said he was proud when fans and media placed him among the best. He told BBC Sport he did not agree that he was the greatest, saying every athlete has their moments and he respected all the legends. In his news conference on Sunday he referred to his total of world titles, saying: "yeah, yeah, yeah, but 10."

Rossi, who retired in 2021, holds the premier-class record of 89 victories. Marquez has 80. Rossi is also the only rider to have won world titles in 125cc, 250cc, 500cc and MotoGP. Agostini has 15 world titles in total, eight of them in the premier class, the last in 1975.
Marquez's contract with Ducati runs until 2028. The season finale is in Valencia.
keyFacts: Marquez clinched the 2026 title in Portimao, Portugal, on Sunday.
He equalled Giacomo Agostini's eight premier-class titles.
He overcame a 102-point deficit, the largest in MotoGP history.
He won seven of 13 grands prix after returning from injury.
Marquez has 10 world titles in all classes; Valentino Rossi has nine.
stories.background: Marquez won six premier-class titles with Honda between 2013 and 2019, then endured years of injuries. He finished 14th in 2023, left Honda for Gresini Racing, the satellite Ducati team, and moved to the factory Ducati squad after a 2024 season with three feature race wins. He won the 2025 title, his first in six years.
stories.whyItMatters: The result puts Marquez level with Agostini's premier-class record and ahead of Rossi on world titles across all classes, which feeds the debate over who is the sport's greatest rider.

stories.headline: South Africa bowl Bangladesh out for 91 on day one of second Test
stories.dek: Marques Ackerman was unbeaten on 46 as the hosts closed on 88 for one at Centurion, three runs behind, after a rain-delayed start.
stories.summary: Marco Jansen and Kagiso Rabada took three wickets each as Bangladesh were bowled out for 91 on day one of the second Test at SuperSport Park. South Africa reached 88 for one by stumps, trailing by three runs.
body: South Africa's pace bowlers dismissed Bangladesh for 91 in 33.3 overs on the first day of the second Test at SuperSport Park, Centurion, on Monday. The hosts were 88 for one at stumps, three runs behind.

Marco Jansen and Kagiso Rabada took three wickets each. Anrich Nortje took two and Simon Harmer one. Both ESPNcricinfo and Sportstar reported it as the lowest first-innings total in a Test at the ground.
Rain delayed the start until 1.40pm, nearly four hours after the scheduled time. South Africa won the toss and chose to field on a well-grassed pitch.
Jansen removed Tanzid Hasan for 3, caught at first slip by Wiaan Mulder. Mahfijul Islam, who top-scored with 23, and Mominul Haque added 34 for the second wicket.

Nortje then bowled Mahfijul and Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto within three balls in his second over. Mulder had Mominul, on 18, play on to his stumps. Jansen got Litton Das, who chased a wide ball and was caught at gully by Zubayr Hamza.

Towhid Hridoy was out for 19 off Harmer on the last ball of the first session. After tea, Rabada took Shoriful Islam, Jaker Ali and Taskin Ahmed in three consecutive overs, a spell of three wickets for one run. Khaled Ahmed then edged Jansen to deep third. Bangladesh lost their last five wickets for six runs.

In reply, captain Aiden Markram and Marques Ackerman put on 49 for the first wicket. Markram was out for 21 off 23 balls, caught behind off Ebadot Hossain; Litton Das took the catch diving forward, according to Cricinfo.

Bangladesh were on the wrong end of an umpiring call. Taskin Ahmed's lbw appeal against Ackerman in the third over was turned down, and Shanto did not review. Replays showed the ball pitched in line and would have hit the stumps. Markram had earlier survived an lbw decision against Shoriful Islam on review.
Hridoy also dropped Hamza at slip off Khaled Ahmed when the batter was on two. Hamza was 9 not out at the close, with Ackerman on 46 including seven fours.
keyFacts: Bangladesh were all out for 91 in 33.3 overs at SuperSport Park, Centurion.
Jansen and Rabada took 3 wickets each; Nortje took 2 and Harmer 1.
Mahfijul Islam top-scored for Bangladesh with 23.
South Africa closed on 88 for 1, with Ackerman 46* and Hamza 9*.
Play began at 1.40pm after a rain delay of nearly four hours.
stories.background: South Africa are looking for a 2-0 series sweep, according to Sportstar. Ackerman scored a century in the first Test, in Johannesburg, where Mahfijul Islam made his Test debut.
stories.whyItMatters: South Africa hold a strong position in the match as they push for a series sweep.
